headline: Advertising's shift to AI-made commercials is raising fears that Britain's next generation of film and TV directors will lose its training ground.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a useful look at AI and creative careers, but a feature built on opinion and one unnamed cost estimate.
importance_line: Young directors and crews who learn on commercial shoots could lose that route, while advertisers gain lower costs, but WPP argues production jobs are not shrinking.
summary: The Guardian reports that the advertising industry's rush to AI is raising fears of a lost generation of British directors, because commercials were a first stage for figures such as Ridley Scott and Guy Ritchie, and one industry source says some AI-made ads cost up to 60% less. WPP, whose new London production facility uses AI, says it sees AI as an enabler and not a threat to production jobs.
notes: Full Guardian text read. The claim of a 'lost generation' is a fear voiced by industry figures, not a measured loss.
